description: Deep and representative ice-core drilling sites of Antarctica and Greenland, compiled for the 3D ICE explorer's Places & Geographic Features. Every position is given by at least two independent sources (coordinate_sources); depths, drilling years, ages and elevations come from the sources in fact_sources, and notes record disagreements between them. scripts/prepare_ice_cores.py builds the explorer catalogues from this table.

conventions.depth_m: Final drilled depth of the core from the surface, in metres.
conventions.reached_bed: True only where a source states that drilling reached the bed (for Vostok, the subglacial lake).
conventions.oldest_ka: For a drilled core, the time span of its continuous dated record, in thousands of years; disturbed ice below it is not counted. For a blue-ice site, the age of its oldest dated ice.
conventions.core_type: deep: about 1000 m or more on a major ice divide or dome; intermediate: about 300–1500 m; shallow: under about 300 m; blue_ice: a blue-ice area sampled at or near the surface.
conventions.coordinates: Decimal degrees on WGS 84, south and west negative.

cross_checked_against.name: Davidge, Brooks & Mah (2022), Global ice drilling and archive location data for select ice cores

sites.name: Vostok
sites.project: Russian Antarctic Expedition deep drilling at Vostok Station (borehole 5G)
sites.operator: Russia (Russian Antarctic Expedition), with French and US science partners

coordinate_sources.what: Vasiliev et al. 2007, Ann. Glaciol. 47, text: Vostok station 78°28'S, 106°48'E, 3488 m a.s.l.
NOAA NCEI paleo study site record 'Vostok' (elev. 3488 m)

reference.citation: Petit et al. 1999, Nature 399, 429–436

sites.notes: Borehole 5G started 20 Feb 1990; drilling stopped at 3623 m in Jan 1998, about 130 m above the lake, and the meteoric-to-accreted (lake) ice transition is at 3538 m (Vasiliev et al. 2007). After deepening via branch hole 5G-2, the drill reached Subglacial Lake Vostok on 5 Feb 2012 at 3769.3 m by ice-core length (Lukin & Vasiliev 2014, Ann. Glaciol. 55(65)). reached_bed=true means the ice-water interface at the base of the ice sheet was reached; there is no bedrock contact. depth_m includes accreted lake ice below 3538 m. oldest_ka=420 is the span of the Petit et al. (1999) climate record, not the age of the deepest (accreted) ice. Discrepancies: NCEI core lengths [36, 40, 2757, 3500] omit 3623/3769 m; the Zenodo 5G row gives bottom 3623 m (1998) and elevation 3500 m vs 3488 m (Vasiliev et al. 2007; NCEI).

sites.project: European Project for Ice Coring in Antarctica (EPICA)

reference.citation: EPICA community members 2004, Nature 429, 623–628

sites.notes: Reported core is EDC2 (EDC99): started 11 Dec 1999, completed 21 Dec 2004 at 3270.2 m, an estimated 16 m above bedrock, stopped because of environmental and drill-safety concerns (Augustin et al. 2007). Parrenin et al. (2007) describe the EDC99 drilling as voluntarily stopped at 3260 m, about 15 m above bedrock, above suspected melt water; Zenodo repository rows give 3259.85 m (IGE) and 3260 m (AWI). The 3260 vs 3270.2 m difference is not explained in the sources consulted; 3270.2 m is the drilling report's final depth. Some secondary sources say '5 m above bedrock', contradicting the drilling report. The first hole, EDC96 (from 1996), was abandoned when the drill stuck at 788 m in 1999. oldest_ka=800 per EDC3 (Parrenin et al. 2007). Discrepancies: NCEI lists core lengths up to 3275 m; the Zenodo IGE row gives elevation 3250 m vs 3233 m (PANGAEA, NCEI). Ten EPICA nations: Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, UK.

sites.project: Allan Hills blue-ice old-ice coring (NSF; Center for Oldest Ice Exploration, COLDEX)
sites.operator: USA (NSF COLDEX; Princeton University, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and partners)

coordinate_sources.what: Shackleton et al. 2025, PNAS 122, main text: ALHIC1901 76.732376°S, 159.356125°E, adjacent to site BIT58/ALHIC1503
USAP-DC dataset 601128 (AH-1503 stable isotopes), spatial coverage point

reference.citation: Shackleton et al. 2025, PNAS 122, e2502681122

sites.notes: One entry for the Allan Hills Main Ice Field (1900–2000 m a.s.l.; drill-site elevation not given, so null). Point and depth are ALHIC1901, drilled to bedrock at 159 m with the IDP 24 cm Blue Ice Drill adjacent to site BIT58/ALHIC1503 (Shackleton et al. 2025); 'drilled' gives 2019–2020 from the core name, while the paper states only that its three cores were drilled in the 2019–20 and 2022–23 seasons. ALHIC1503 (2015–16 season) yielded basal ice with 40Ar_atm ages to 2.7 Ma (Yan et al. 2019, Nature 574, 663–666); the BIT58 hole was first drilled to 124 m in 2011–12 (USAP-DC 601128). oldest_ka=6000 is the oldest dated ice in the area: up to ~6 Ma (Late Miocene), dated by the deficit of 40Ar relative to the modern atmosphere, from ALHIC1902 (76.745357°S, 159.374108°E, ~1.5 km SE; drilled to bedrock at 206 m); ALHIC1901 reaches the Early Pliocene. The ice is stratigraphically discontinuous (snapshots, not a continuous record); samples older than ~2.7 Ma show Ar loss, and gas-poor basal ice beneath the 6 Ma sample is undated. 1 Ma ice was first reported from the base of a 126 m core (Higgins et al. 2015). Not in the NCEI or Zenodo files.
